sourceLesson: Backend LLD: OOP-3: Inheritance, MRO and Polymorphism

questions.title: MRO Search Order
questions.question: For class D(B, C) where B and C both inherit from A, in what order does Python search for a method called on a D() instance?

questions.title: Understanding super() Semantics
questions.question: super() in a multiple-inheritance chain refers to:

options.optionText: The next class in the current object's MRO after the class where super() is written

questions.title: isinstance vs type Check
questions.question: Given class A: pass, class B(A): pass, an object b = B(). Which is True?

options.optionText: isinstance(b, A) → True and type(b) == A → False

questions.title: Duck Typing With Drones
questions.question: Uber's dispatch(vehicle) calls vehicle.start(). If a totally unrelated Drone class (not inheriting from Vehicle) has a .start() method, what does Python's duck typing say?

options.optionText: TypeError — Drone is not a Vehicle
Works fine — Python only checks that .start() exists on the passed object

questions.title: Redefined Method Overwrite
Missing eq/hash Method
questions.question: A Zone class defines __lt__ by area. Which of these will NOT work out of the box?

options.optionText: zone in some_set (membership test on a set of Zones)

questions.title: Cooperative Init Chain Behavior
questions.question: In cooperative multiple inheritance with **kwargs-passing super().__init__ calls, the shared top-most ancestor's __init__:

options.optionText: Runs once per parent that inherits it (twice in a diamond)
Runs exactly once, because everyone follows the same MRO chain
Runs only if explicitly called by name

questions.title: Overload Dispatch Comparison
questions.question: Which best distinguishes Java overloading from Python's @singledispatch?

options.optionText: Java at compile time based on declared types; @singledispatch at runtime based on actual argument type
@singledispatch dispatches on all arguments, not just the first

questions.title: Skipped Parent Constructor Call
Unhashable Type After eq
questions.question: Defining __eq__ on a class without also defining __hash__ causes:

options.optionText: Instances of the class become unhashable — cannot be used in set or as dict keys

questions.title: Method Resolution Order (MRO)
questions.question: Given the hierarchy class A: pass, class B(A): pass, class C(A): pass, class D(B, C): pass, what does D.__mro__ show (ignoring object)? Apply C3 merge — parents in written order, and any ancestor appears after all its descendants.

questions.title: Duck Typing Silent Bug
questions.question: In Uber's dispatch code, a function dispatch(vehicle) calls vehicle.start(). A colleague passes in an EmailNotification object (unrelated to Vehicle) which happens to have a .start() method that marks the email as "sending". No error is raised and the email gets marked as sending. Which best explains this per duck typing?

options.optionText: Python auto-converted the object into a Vehicle
Python only checks whether the method exists on the object at runtime, never what the method means — so wrong-object-right-name bugs run silently
dispatch should have raised a TypeError and this is a Python bug
EmailNotification must secretly inherit from Vehicle

questions.title: Missing Super Init Call

options.optionText: AttributeError — Bike.__init__ never calls super().__init__(), so reg was never set

questions.title: Diamond Inheritance Method Resolution
questions.question: In the diamond class EC(EV, CV) where EV and CV both define get_priority_score() differently (20 and 30), and EC defines nothing, what does EC().get_priority_score() return, and why?

options.optionText: 20 — EV comes before CV in EC's MRO, and Python stops at the first class that defines the method
Returns the sum (50) — Python merges both

questions.title: Method Overloading Myth
questions.question:
What will be the output:

```python
class Fare:
    def calc(self, dist): return 10*dist
    def calc(self, dist, surge): return 10*dist*surge
f = Fare()
print(f.calc(5))
```

options.optionText: Prints 50 — Python picks the 1-arg version by overloading
TypeError — the second def replaced the first (Python has no overloading), so calc now needs 2 args
